Tanya: "We shipped the async decision widget. Velocity was 23 points, highest this quarter. The Zephyr integration was the key unlock."

payload.focus: Tanya's sprint retro: async decision widget shipped, velocity 23 points highest this quarter, Zephyr integration as key unlock
payload.rationale: This short sprint retro touches three load-bearing areas: the zero-effort-capture narrative (the async decision widget), the Zephyr integration position (DependenciesIntegrations), and the velocity KPI (KPIsSuccess). I expanded the AntiSlack positioning narrative and PositioningThesis because Tanya's claim that the widget shipped is a thesis-validation event the passes must bind to. I included both pricing positions ($12 and $15 tier) and PackagingEntitlement because the Sprint 4 retro source already links pricing updates to this sprint context. The webhook architecture and stack overview were expanded since the Zephyr integration is an architecture-level decision. Style observations (ToneDirectPersonal, ToneAuthoritative) were included because the document uses the same direct-quote and metric-anchored register as the existing Sprint 4 retro. Notably, the existing Obs_TinaVelocity attributes the 23-point velocity claim to Tina, while this document has Tanya stating it — the passes need that observation in context to detect the speaker discrepancy. I did not expand Segmentation or Narrative_DecisionsEvaporate beyond their parent positions, as the document does not surface segmentation or decision-loss themes directly.

^-marked entries are compressed stubs carrying child addresses. Their narration and any surfaced witness quotes are verbatim-accurate — quote them as-is — but a stub carries no provenance (source, date, supersession). Expand (aswritten_expand with the IRIs you need) before any claim that turns on WHEN or by WHOM something was said, or whether it is still the current framing. Witness-depth sections below already carry full provenance.

Deciding where to go: each mapped area's narration tells you the SPAN of what lives under it; the area index names everything else. Expand a subtree when its narration (or name) shows your subject plausibly lives there — you'll get the trajectory, the variants, and the verbatim witness. But be strict about absence: if neither the map's narrations nor the index's names substantively cover your subject, it is NOT in this perspective — say so rather than expanding a loose thematic match (a word-overlap is not coverage). Decide from the map; expand to ground.
